subject.title: [improvement] Sub-agent cascade circuit breaker for multi-agent team reliability

question: What sub-agent breaker contract should OpenClaw core own before implementation: a dedicated per-agent/task breaker, integration into the broader session-health breaker track, or deferral to existing narrower guards?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the permanent behavior crosses config schema, persisted runtime state, spawn admission policy, failure taxonomy, notification routing, operator recovery, and overlap with other breaker proposals, so automation cannot safely choose the product contract.

options.title: Design dedicated subagent health receipts
options.body: Define a core receipt keyed by target agent and task signature, with failure class, counters, cooldown or half-open state, manual reset, and sessions_spawn error semantics before implementation.

options.title: Fold into session-health breaker work
options.body: Treat subagent cascade protection as one consumer of the broader unhealthy-session breaker in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62615, accepting that subagent-specific UI and task-signature semantics may wait.

options.title: Defer to narrower guards
options.body: Keep provider, session, tool-loop, cron, and subagent concurrency guards separate and revisit this request only if a narrower missing API remains after those land.

recommendation.title: Design dedicated subagent health receipts
recommendation.body: Define a core receipt keyed by target agent and task signature, with failure class, counters, cooldown or half-open state, manual reset, and sessions_spawn error semantics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter introduced sessions_spawn and recently maintained the subagent registry/spawn boundary, making him the best available owner for the product contract choice.
